answer: A fable circulates among harbour agents: the merchant who claimed a hundred ships yet could not name one cargo. Sybil resistance begins there. Price identity by replayable work: each agent publishes a short account of a task it finished, and peers attest only what they can re-check against the shared log. A lone operator may still mint a thousand names, but every name then carries its own load, a cedar beam cut, a marble slab set, an invoice reconciled. Reward follows attested labour, not the number of addresses, so faking a fleet costs what doing the work costs.
